controls.profile_surplus_help: Follows the sun: starts and stops on solar surplus, never charging past the SoC cap.
controls.profile_power_latch_help: Starts once total solar production hits the threshold, then charges to the target SoC without stopping — may draw from the grid once production dips.
controls.profile_surplus_latch_help: Starts only once genuine export surplus hits the threshold, then charges to the target SoC without stopping.
controls.latch_compare_body: Both PV power and Surplus (latch) are "charge to completion" modes: once started, they keep charging at full power through a dip in the trigger, stopping only at the target SoC. They differ only in what starts them — PV power reacts to total solar production and may pull from the grid, while Surplus (latch) reacts only to genuine leftover power after the house (battery discharge doesn't count as surplus). Fail-safes (stale data, disconnect, override, SoC cap) always take priority over either mode.
controls.hours_hint: Leave hours empty for a permanent override until changed.

setup.title: Secure access — wha
setup.secure_intro: Installing wha as an app and enabling offline support both require a secure (HTTPS) connection. If this deployment runs behind a reverse proxy with an internal certificate authority (e.g. Caddy's tls internal), trust its root certificate below on each device you use.
setup.secure_warning: A website cannot silently install a root certificate into your device's trust store — every platform requires a few manual taps to install and confirm trust. The steps below are the shortest path per device.
setup.no_ca_body: No CA root certificate is configured for this deployment (web.caRootPath is unset) — this is expected for local development or a setup without a reverse proxy. If you're already on https:// or localhost, you can skip straight to "%s" below.
setup.ios_step1: Download the iOS/macOS configuration profile above in Safari.
setup.ios_step2: Open Settings → General → VPN & Device Management and tap the downloaded profile.
setup.ios_step3: Tap Install, then Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings and enable full trust for the "wha secure access root CA" certificate.
setup.ios_step4: Reload the wha dashboard in Safari, then use the Share sheet → Add to Home Screen.
setup.android_step1: Download the root certificate above in Chrome.
setup.android_step2: Open Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate and select the downloaded file.
setup.android_step3: Reload the wha dashboard in Chrome; when the install banner or menu shows Install app, tap it.
setup.macos_step1: Download the root certificate above, or run the helper script: scripts/trust-ca.sh.
setup.macos_step2: If installing manually, open it in Keychain Access, add it to the System keychain, then double-click it and set Trust → Always Trust.
setup.windows_step1: Download the root certificate above, or run the helper script as Administrator: scripts/trust-ca.ps1.
setup.windows_step2: If installing manually, double-click the file, choose Local Machine → Trusted Root Certification Authorities, then finish the wizard.
setup.linux_step1: Run the helper script: scripts/trust-ca.sh (copies the cert to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and runs update-ca-certificates).
setup.install_body: Once the connection is trusted (or you're on localhost), reload this dashboard and use your browser's install prompt — or the Share sheet's "Add to Home Screen" on iOS — to add wha to your home screen. It launches full-screen and keeps a basic offline shell if the connection drops.
